 Live Updates: Top moments, highlights and stats from our season tipoff tripleheader on NBC and Peacock
 The Detroit Pistons face the Boston Celtics (3 p.m. ET) followed by Knicks hosting the 76ers and Thunder facing the Spurs.
 Ben Lambert, for NBA.com
 Updated on October 21, 2026 4:07 AM VIctor Wembanyama and Chet Holmgren are facing off as the Spurs host the Thunder on NBC & Peacock.
 All-Access Coverage: Celtics at Pistons 
 All-Access Coverage: 76ers at Knicks 
 All-Access Coverage: Thunder at Spurs 
 The NBA is back! Our 81st season is underway with a tripleheader on NBC and Peacock. Follow the live blog for all details through the night.
 What we know about NBA American Express Tip-Off:
 The Pistons came back from 22-down to defeat the Celtics 121-113 , led by a second half surge from Duncan Robinson (21 pts) and Javonte Green (19 second-half points).
 The Knicks raised their championship banner at Madison Square Garden, celebrating their first title in 53 years.
 The Philadelphia 76ers opened the season with a 106-100 win over the Knicks, as Tyrese Maxey (28 pts), Jaylen Brown (19 pts), LeBron James (14 pts, 9 reb, 7 ast, 1 stl, 1 blk) and Joel Embiid (13 pts, 11 reb, 6 ast, 3 blk, 2 stl) showed chemistry in their debut together.
 Now, tonight’s action concludes with a rematch of the epic Western Conference Finals, with the Oklahoma City Thunder visiting the San Antonio Spurs (9:30 p.m. ET, NBC/Peacock).
 11:53 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Thunder lead 93-80 after three
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (28 pts) has been the best player in this Western Conference Finals rematch, leading the Thunder to a double-digit lead as the fourth quarter looms.
 SGA’s stepback midrange game has been on point — it’s nigh-unguardable when he’s fading away and got it flowing. Shades of Paul Pierce or Kobe Bryant. He can rise and fire at any time.
 Can San Antonio mount one more charge? Tune in to NBC and Peacock to find out.
 11:43 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Mara mayhem for OKC
 Thunder 84, Spurs 70 with 4:11 to go in the third. 
 No. 12 pick Aday Mara (5 pts) flashed for the Thunder here, showing the impact of his 7-foot-3 frame.
 Aday Mara MAKING PLAYS in his first NBA game 🔥
 Big-time swat at the rim.
Two-hand alley-oop slam.
 The Thunder lead in Q3! pic.twitter.com/YJpmoBAm8J 
 — NBA (@NBA) October 21, 2026 
 11:31 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Wembanyama’s everywhere for a moment
 Thunder 76, Spurs 67 with 5:49 to go in the third. 
 Victor Wembanyama (8 pts, 7 reb, 5 blk) just dove to the floor to tap a loose ball, then leapt to his feet to race into the lane to block a layup from Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, as the Spurs get back into the contest.
 He was fired up afterwards — this matchup matters.
 11:19 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Spurs cut into the lead
 Thunder 68, Spurs 53 with 9:53 to go in the third. 
 A 9-0 run has San Antonio back in the mix to open the third quarter, as Stephon Castle (8 pts) sticks a 3-pointer off an assist from De’Aaron Fox.
 10:57 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Thunder lead 65-44 at the half
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (16 pts, 4 ast) is pacing the Thunder attack in the Frost Bank Center, as OKC overwhelms San Antonio to take a 19-point lead at the break.
 SGA AND-1 😤
 Showcases the handles.
Sinks the TOUGH jumper. 
 He's got a game-high 16 PTS as the Thunder lead at the break! pic.twitter.com/6k92rv1VP5 
 — NBA (@NBA) October 21, 2026 
 “They’re a really good team,” said Jaylen Williams (5 pts, 6 reb). “You’ve got to put a lot more effort into loose balls, plays like that.”
 Victor Wembanyama (8 pts, 6 reb) found some offense towards the end of the half, becoming the top scorer for the Spurs, along with Julian Champagnie (8 pts, 2 3PM).
 But it’s been basically all OKC in this rematch of the 2025 Western Conference Finals.
 “The depth, the defense, and the shot-making from this Thunder team. Everyone contributing; making it a little personal in this first half,” said NBC’s Grant Hill. “Textbook half from OKC.”
 10:47 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 OKC controlling the flow
 Thunder 51, Spurs 33 with 4:33 to go in the second. 
 San Antonio’s down to 12-for-43 (27.9%) shooting from the field, as Oklahoma City locks down.
 No one’s loose for the Spurs — Julian Champagnie (8 pts) is their high scorer. On the other end, the Thunder have flashed their depth — all 11 OKC players who have played have scored.
 10:34 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Thunder with a shooting display
 Thunder 46, Spurs 30 with 8:08 to go in the second. 
 Oklahoma City’s now 7-for-8 (87.5%) from 3-point range on the contest, as Kenrich Williams (3 pts, 1 3PM) knocks one down, speeding them to a lead over San Antonio.
 The Spurs are 3-for-14 (21.4%) from distance so far.
 10:26 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Wembanyama with the eraser
 Thunder 37, Spurs 28 with 9:21 to go in the second. 
 Victor Wembanyama (1 blk) just shut down a layup attempt by Ajay Mitchell in transition.
 Wemby's first block of the 2026-27 NBA season 👽
 Times it up.
Swats it off the glass. pic.twitter.com/xNbgTZDaCw 
 — NBA (@NBA) October 21, 2026 
 He came into the game with 627 career rejections — 13th most in NBA history for a player after three seasons. Mark Eaton has the most, with 1,082; Spurs legend David Robinson is second with 944.
 Wembanyama and Jaylin Williams were just jawing at each other after Chet Holmgren fell to the floor after clashing with De’Aaron Fox. Feels like Game 8 indeed.
 “This is a heated rivalry, a Playoff atmosphere,” said NBC’s Grant Hill.
 10:16 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 OKC leads 34-28 after the first
 Jared McCain (8 pts, 2 3PM) and Alex Caruso (6 pts, 2 3PM) are perfect from deep so far, complementing Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (9 pts, 3 ast) as our final game of the evening opens in San Antonio.
 Both were big in Oklahoma City’s wins in the 2025 Western Conference Finals, and seem to have settled right back in tonight, which NBC’s Grant Hill suggested felt like “Game 8” between the two teams.
 Eight Spurs have scored on the other end, led by Stephon Castle and Julian Champagnie, who have five points apiece.
 9:59 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Sixers ride new core to 106-100 win
 Tyrese Maxey (28 pts) | Jaylen Brown (19 pts, 8 reb, 6 ast) | LeBron James (14 pts, 9 reb, 7 ast, 1 blk, 1 stl) | Joel Embiid (13 pts, 11 reb, 6 ast, 3 blk, 2 stl) 
 The Sixers’ star-studded core, led by Tyrese Maxey, took control late as the Sixers knocked off the defending champion Knicks on ring night at Madison Square Garden.
 Watch highlights from the game here 
 Jaylen Brown and LeBron James chipped in around the edges, as did Joel Embiid. Philly’s new core had palpable chemistry in their first game together.
 LeBron James and Jaylen Brown make their Philly debuts, @sixers open the season with a W ‼️ @KingJames : 14 PTS, 9 REB, 7 AST @FCHWPO : 19 PTS, 8 REB, 6 AST pic.twitter.com/0tdCrZBsLP 
 — NBA (@NBA) October 21, 2026 
 “I like the way we played. I think we played exceptionally well, especially defensively,” said James. “Good win to start the season.”
 With the win, LeBron raised his all-time record to 25-10 in MSG.
 Jalen Brunson (21 pts on 6-for-19 FGA) was the top scorer for the Knicks, but couldn’t get loose down the stretch as Philly surged.
 Karl-Anthony Towns (19 pts, 12 reb, 2 blk, 3 3PM) had a strong stretch in the fourth, but Mikal Bridges (4 pts) and OG Anunoby (10 pts, 5 reb) played below their standard.
 “The Sixers head back down I-95 to South Philly 1-0,” said NBC’s Mike Tirico.
 9:45 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Passion in the Garden
 Sixers 104, Knicks 98 with 1:52 to go in the fourth. 
 Both teams are into it as the clock winds down in MSG.
 Karl-Anthony Towns (19 pts, 11 reb, 3 3PM) and Joel Embiid (13 pts, 11 reb, 5 ast, 2 stl, 2 3PM) just traded 3-pointers, with KAT pulling up from 28 feet to drill one from the top of the arc.
 Jalen Brunson (19 pts on 5-for-17 FGA) has been grinding to find his offense, dealing with the size of Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe.
 9:39 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Alvarado ups the energy
 Sixers 96, Knicks 92 with 5:36 to go in the fourth. 
 Jose Alvarado (8 pts, 3 ast, 2 stl) has kept the energy pumping for the Knicks with Jalen Brunson on the bench, helping them hang around as Kentavious Caldwell-Pope (6 pts, 2 3PM) gets loose for Philly.
 Alvarado’s an old-school point guard offensively — his head is up, his dribble is live, and he’s looking to do what the team needs on the possession.
 9:34 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Tyrese tears down floor
 Sixers 90, Knicks 86 with 7:52 to go in the fourth. 
 An example of the Sixers’ potency in transition. Few players are more dangerous with a step than Tyrese Maxey (26 pts).
 STOPS ➡️ BUCKETS
 Joel Embiid (3 BLK) protects the rim on one end and Tyrese Maxey (24 PTS) converts the and-1 on the other!
 Watch PHI/NYK 4Q action on NBC and Peacock. pic.twitter.com/5o2CtXrMDY 
 — NBA (@NBA) October 21, 2026 
 9:16 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Sixers up 83-76 after three
 Jaylen Brown (19 pts) knocked down back-to-back 3-pointers to give the Sixers the lead heading into the fourth quarter, capping an 11-0 run. They won the quarter by that margin, 29-18.
 Philly’s tough to deal with in basically any phase of the game — lot of scoring talent on the floor.
 The Knicks are scrapping, but Karl-Anthony Towns (9 pts, 7 reb) and OG Anunoby (7 pts on 2-for-10 FGA) have largely been outplayed. We’ll see if they have a response on ring night at Madison Square Garden.
 9:08 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Knicks’ core responds
 Knicks 76, Sixers 72 with 3:00 to go in the third. 
 Josh Hart, Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns are taking over the second half of the third quarter for the Knicks, fending off a charge by the Sixers.
 They have the last 13 points for New York.
 Anfernee Simons (10 pts) is keeping the Sixers’ offense afloat with LeBron James on the bench. He’s a meaningful piece — a microwave scorer wherever he goes.
 Philly’s basically played seven players so far, with limited cameos from Adem Bona and Jabari Walker as well.
 We’ll see if Nick Nurse can find another player to keep in the mix — Justin Edwards and Caleb Love both had their moments last season.
 8:59 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 The Sixers on the break
 Knicks 63, Sixers 62 with 7:55 to go in the third quarter. 
 Eight straight fast break points for Philadelphia to open the second half, capped by back-to-back finishes at the rim from LeBron James (9 pts, 4 reb, 5 ast, 2 stl).
 Jaylen Brown and LeBron James connect on back-to-back buckets!
 1-point game in the 3Q from MSG… pic.twitter.com/kNR1nBlNka 
 — NBA (@NBA) October 21, 2026 
 They’re going to be a force in transition once they start clicking, given Tyrese Maxey’s speed and the athleticism on the wing.
 Classic LeBron team moments here.
 8:34 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Knicks lead 58-54 at the half
 Jalen Brunson (15 pts) and Andre Drummond (10 pts, 12 reb, 3 ast, 2 blk) have New York up at the break, out-dueling Tyrese Maxey (16 pts) and Joel Embiid (10 pts, 2 stl).
 Drummond, a former Sixer, made his presence felt on the glass, going toe-to-toe with Embiid on multiple occasions.
 He’s helped the Knicks to a 25-8 advantage in bench points.
 “I’m tired of the preseason. I’m ready for the real thing,” said Drummond. “It’s a lot of fun out there tonight.”
 8:24 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 JB & LBJ on the attack
 Knicks 54, Sixers 50 with 1:00 to go in the second. 
 Jaylen Brown (9 pts) and LeBron James (5 pts, 4 reb, 4 ast) just combined for six straight points, culminating with a dunk from JB to cut the Knicks lead to four.
 LeBron James with the pass, Jaylen Brown with the finish 💥
 4-point game at the break on NBC and Peacock! pic.twitter.com/ZiSl77DgSb 
 — NBA (@NBA) October 21, 2026 
 There’s some chemistry between LeBron and his new star wing teammate — shades of Dwyane Wade, maybe?
 8:01 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Clarkson to the rack
 Knicks 40, Sixers 30 with 7:25 to go in the second. 
 Jordan Clarkson (4 pts) just scored back-to-back buckets for the Knicks, including snaking to the rim off an Andre Drummond screen to force a Philadelphia timeout.
 Clarkson’s now in his 12th season, averaging 15.3 ppg for his career. He spent part of the 2018 season as a teammate of LeBron James in Cleveland.
 7:57 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 The impact of Alvarado
 Knicks 32, Sixers 28 with 9:15 to go in the second. 
 Jose Alvarado just dropped off a dime to Andre Drummond (10 pts, 11 reb), stole the ball from Jaylen Brown at midcourt and pushed it for a 3-pointer in transition.
 THIS. KNICKS. SEQUENCE.
 Jose Alvarado (5 PTS, 2-3 FGM), Andre Drummond (10 PTS, 11 REB) and the @nyknicks lead in the 2Q on NBC and Peacock 🗽 pic.twitter.com/ZHFyBDQSeQ 
 — NBA (@NBA) October 21, 2026 
 A signature energy play from the Brooklyn-born point guard.
 7:49 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Knicks lead 25-23 after one
 Andre Drummond (6 pts, 6 reb, 1 stl, 1 blk) put his stamp on the first quarter, crashing the glass against his former team to help the Knicks to a two-point lead at the quarter break.
 New York has 16 points in the paint to eight for Philadelphia.
 The game saw three lead changes and three ties in the first period.
 7:43 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 LeBron in the record books
 Sixers 22, Knicks 19 with 1:56 to go in the first. 
 The King has his first points as a Philadelphia 76er, clearing out space against Landry Shamet for the layup. A strong catch and finish.
 LeBron James' first bucket in his @sixers debut 🙌 pic.twitter.com/HJT7u54qee 
 — NBA (@NBA) October 20, 2026 
 7:40 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Wemby in the spot
 Victor Wembanyama is debonair in the grey-and-blue suit ahead of tonight’s contest against the Oklahoma City Thunder (9:30 ET, NBC/Peacock).
 Last season's Kia NBA DPOY has arrived 👽
 Wemby and the @spurs start their 2026-27 campaign against the Thunder at 9:30pm/et on NBC & Peacock! pic.twitter.com/IHUoigDCCf 
 — NBA (@NBA) October 20, 2026 
 7:33 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 The Maxey-LeBron two man game
 Sixers 14, Knicks 14 with 4:36 to go in the first. 
 Tyrese Maxey (8 pts) drilled a midrange jumper while fading into the corner, shaking Jalen Brunson with a screen and give-and-go dish from LeBron James (3 ast).
 That should be a strong element of the offense for the Sixers. LeBron’s ability to read the floor is second-to-none, and Maxey is a blur finding and exploiting space.
 7:21 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Maxey starts on the attack
 Sixers 8, Knicks 5 with 8:58 to go in the first. 
 Tyrese Maxey (6 pts) opens the new season with back-to-back 3-pointers, including a confident one from above-the-break in transition.
 Jaylen Brown (2 pts) got in the ledger off a feed from LeBron James, following a 3-pointer on the wing from Jalen Brunson, who stepped to the arc and seized the opportunity after Maxey was knocked to the floor by a screen.
 LeBron James finds Jaylen Brown for his first bucket as a 76er! 👀
 📺 NBA Tip-Off on NBC & Peacock pic.twitter.com/6BVdELkvur 
 — NBA on NBC and Peacock (@NBAonNBC) October 20, 2026 
 6:58 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 The Captain speaks
 rings acquired 🔥 pic.twitter.com/6XpZuJ36BY 
 — NEW YORK KNICKS (@nyknicks) October 20, 2026 
 Ring on his finger, Jalen Brunson credited the fans for sticking with them, including in Game 4 of the 2025 NBA Finals, when they rallied from 29-down to win on a tip-in by OG Anunoby.
 “This is unbelievable. This is really a dream come true,” said Brunson. “The joy that this city had this summer, we’d love to replicate that again.”
 The fans chanted “let’s go Knicks” as the banner honoring the 2025-26 NBA Champions was raised to the top of Madison Square Garden.
 6:47 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 A ring ceremony in New York City
 The Knicks are raising an NBA championship banner to the rafters in Madison Square Garden for the first time in 53 years, as fans applaud the hustle, tenacity and skill of the 2025-26 team, our reigning champions.
 Ben Stiller shares what the Knicks championship means to New York. 🧡 pic.twitter.com/OAYfioBONo 
 — NBA on NBC and Peacock (@NBAonNBC) October 20, 2026 
 There are legends in the building; the crowd is warm and appreciative; Mike Breen is on the mic.
 Tune in to NBC and Peacock for this special occasion.
 5:36 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Pistons win 121-113
 Paul George (38 pts) | Duncan Robinson (21 pts, 15 in the fourth ) | Javonte Green (19 second-half points) 
 Detroit controlled the glass and caught fire from 3-point range to storm back and beat the Celtics at Little Caesars Arena, completing the largest opening-day comeback in 30 years.
 Watch highlights from the game here 
 “We had a good talk at halftime, and we lit that fire a little bit better,” said Cade Cunningham (16 pts).
 The Pistons grabbed 59 rebounds to 45 for the Celtics, helping them earn a 44-34 advantage in points in the paint.
 They also shot 11-for-22 (50%) from distance in the second half, led by Robinson and Green, who each had five 3-pointers.
 On the other end, the Celtics offense bogged down, with Jayson Tatum (13 pts on 6-for-23 FGA) unable to get to the rim to complement a big day from Paul George, although he added 11 assists in the game.
 “This Pistons team has a ton of fight in them,” said NBC’s Brian Scalabrine.
 The Celtics were the last team to come back from 20+ down on opening day. They did so in 1997, rallying to beat the eventual champion Chicago Bulls.
 5:29 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 One last surge from Boston
 Pistons 114, Celtics 110 with 1:06 remaining. 
 Jayson Tatum (13 pts, 11 ast) found Paul George (38 pts) for a wing 3-pointer on the break, capping an 11-2 run to give the Celtics a breath of life.
 But Detroit has the ball with less than a minute to go.
 5:17 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 ‘On fire here in the fourth’
 Pistons 107, Celtics 99 with 5:10 to go in the fourth. 
 Detroit’s seized their biggest lead of the game with an 18-0 run, led by Duncan Robinson (23 pts, 5 3PM), who is going crazy in the season opener.
 Robinson just called for more noise from the crowd as the Celtics were forced into a timeout.
 Boston looks a step slow, while Detroit’s playing with pace and energy.
 5:13 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Can’t lose Duncan
 Pistons 101, Celtics 99 with 6:14 to go in the game. 
 Sam Hauser just fouled Duncan Robinson (17 pts) on a 3-point attempt, bringing Detroit within one.
 Daniss Jenkins pushed it into the paint, then tossed the rock out over traffic to Ausar Thompson, who flipped it to Robinson flying out of the corner. He rose up with Hauser trailing, drawing the foul with a bump to the body.
 On the next possession, Robinson found Javonte Green (14 pts, +21) for another 3-pointer, giving the Pistons their first lead since it was 34-33.
 5:09 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Robinson on the arc
 Celtics 99, Pistons 95 with 7:34 to go in the game. 
 Duncan Robinson (14 pts, 4 3PM) just drilled a 3-pointer to force a timeout, sending the Detroit crowd into ecstatics as these teams go back-and-forth to open the season.
 Pistons fans are going nuts after this ferocious block and Duncan Robinson triple!
 📺 NBA Tip-Off on NBC & Peacock pic.twitter.com/knXTyPCG5e 
 — NBA on NBC and Peacock (@NBAonNBC) October 20, 2026 
 He has the last eight points for Detroit, helping them strike back after Boston opened another 10-point lead.
 5:01 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Robinson on the roll
 A triple-high screen just freed Mitchell Robinson for an alley-oop from Derrick White. Heck of a set from Joe Mazzulla.
 Baylor Scheierman brushed past before this clip begins, giving the action a distinctive look.
 Derrick White finds the cutting Mitchell Robinson for the alley-oop!
 📺 NBA Tip-Off on NBC & Peacock pic.twitter.com/F0ZlzIrz3j 
 — NBA on NBC and Peacock (@NBAonNBC) October 20, 2026 
 “I’ve been in the league 25 years,” said NBC’s Brian Scalabrine. “I don’t know if I’ve ever seen that.”
 4:55 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Celtics lead 88-82 after three
 Baylor Scheierman knocked down a 3-pointer with 0.2 left on the clock, lifting Boston to a two-possession lead off another dime from Jayson Tatum (11 pts, 10 ast).
 Detroit won the third quarter 37-30, cutting into a lead that reached 22 points.
 “(We’re) not allowing them to get comfortable and going where they were going to go,” said Pistons assistant coach Jarrett Jack.
 The Pistons’ hustle is up against the Celtics’ passing as we enter the final period in the first NBA game of the season. Get to NBC and Peacock to watch the battle!
 4:51 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Pistons on the hunt
 Celtics 81, Pistons 77 with 2:32 to go in the third. 
 Two more 3-pointers for Javonte Green (11 pts) have the Celtics on their heels, as the Pistons are on rolling downhill.
 Detroit’s made five of their last seven 3-pointers to get back in it.
 4:44 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Green means go
 Celtics 78, Pistons 69 with 4:40 to go in the third. 
 Javonte Green (5 pts) has provided instant impact to get the Pistons back in it, bringing life to the fans at Little Caesars Arena.
 He just knocked down a corner 3-pointer to bring Detroit, which is on a 19-6 run, back within single digits.
 The Pistons are showing fire in responding to the Celtics’ charge. We’ve got a good one as the season begins!
 4:39 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 More history for PG
 Celtics 77, Pistons 64 with 5:33 to go in the third. 
 “What kind of bucket do you want?” NBC’s Terry Gannon just intoned. “Paul George will give it to you right now.”
 George just hit an acrobatic and-one layup, bouncing off the contest from Jalen Duren and tossing the ball off the glass with his right hand.
 PG (31 pts) now has the most points for a Celtic in their debut.
 Detroit’s battling back in front of their home crowd, though, led by Cade Cunningham (14 pts).
 4:34 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Paul George raining from deep
 Celtics 72, Pistons 52 with 7:59 to go in the third. 
 Three straight 3-pointers for Paul George (28 pts, 6-for-8 3PA, 4 stl), who is putting on a show on NBC.
 Paul George is going OFF from deep with three triples in a row. 🔥
 📺 NBA Tip-Off on NBC & Peacock pic.twitter.com/2neSOci33Q 
 — NBA on NBC and Peacock (@NBAonNBC) October 20, 2026 
 The 37-year-old wing looks spry today.
 JB Bickerstaff has countered with former Celtic Javonte Green, who will bring some athleticism and hustle on the wing.
 4:29 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 A quick timeout for Detroit
 Celtics 63, Pistons 47 with 10:36 to go in the third. 
 JB Bickerstaff called a halt to the action after Derrick White (8 pts, 2-for-5 3PA) hit an uncontested 3-pointer from the the top of the arc, giving Boston a quick 5-0 run.
 Their ball movement is giving Detroit problems at this point — there’s a lot of ground to cover.
 “The Celtics have so many weapons out there,” said NBC’s Brian Scalabrine. “If they have their spacing right, they’re going to be tough to stop.”
 “Detroit has no more room for awareness mistakes,” said NBC’s Robbie Hummel, relaying Bickerstaff’s comments to his team. “They’ve got to lock in on both ends.”
 4:19 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 The King steps in
 A dapper LeBron James has arrived at Madison Square Garden to begin the campaign. The 76ers face the Knicks in the second game of our triple-header.
 LEBRON ARRIVES FOR HIS SIXERS DEBUT ‼️ @KingJames begins his NBA-record Year 24 TONIGHT against the Knicks at 7pm/et on NBC and Peacock 🍿 pic.twitter.com/zL3y8JZejy 
 — NBA (@NBA) October 20, 2026 
 4:17 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 History for PG
 Paul George’s latest 3-pointer brought him into eighth place on the all-time charts with 2,551, passing Kyle Korver .
 With this triple, Paul George moves into 8TH ALL-TIME in three-pointers made 🤩
 He's got a game-high 17 points as the Celtics lead at the break on NBC and Peacock! pic.twitter.com/edc8Da381c 
 — NBA (@NBA) October 20, 2026 
 4:13 p.m. ET / OCT 20
 Celtics lead 58-45 at the half
 Kevin Huerter’s attempt at a buzzer-beating 3-pointer was waved off, as Jayson Tatum and Paul George (17 pts, 3 3PM, 3 reb, 2 stl) doubled Cade Cunningham, harassing him into a late cross-court pass to preserve the 13-point lead.
 Boston broke away with its defense in the second quarter. Detroit’s down to 38.6% FG shooting, including a 4-for-18 (22%) mark from deep.
